scope: Gate wave 1; only the six assigned spectral/interval/composite boundary subjects. No whole-item acceptance.

boundaries.evidence: Step 5.2 has q=exp(-2 kappa a)>0 for the stated a,kappa>0. At delta=0 its exact difference identity gives T=(4/C)q and zero error; no division by delta occurs. Steps 2.1 and 5.1 allow r=0. The denominators C and 1+delta are positive under the stated hypotheses and eta<1, respectively.
Steps 2.1 and 3.1 match values and derivatives at x=0 and x=a. Step 5.2 controls the thick-barrier limit q down to 0 and permits the error-bound endpoint |delta|=1/2 with |1+delta|>=1/2.

For f=0 the functional and both resolvents vanish by linearity in steps 2.1 and 3.1. Step 4.1 explicitly gives K_z=0 when alpha=0. For alpha nonzero the witness f=conjugate(G_z) has ell_z(f)=||G_z||_2^2>0.
Step 4.1 proves range K_z is contained in C G_z, has rank exactly one if alpha!=0, and is zero if alpha=0; its norm claim is the displayed upper bound, not an asserted exact norm.
Step 1.1 proves 1+alpha/(2k)!=0 for nonreal z and real alpha. Re(k)>0 also excludes k=0. Step 4.1 separately includes alpha=0 without dividing by alpha.

Step 2.1 evaluates the free resolvent at the interface, r(0)=ell_z(f), and uses the derivative jump supplied by F1 to construct the delta-domain preimage. Step 3.1 identifies it with the actual resolvent.

AC and CC are retained in the Statement for the declared self-adjoint/free-resolvent interfaces F1. Step 2.1 constructs the preimage explicitly, step 3.1 uses injectivity, and step 4.1 uses the stated Cauchy-Schwarz norm interface F2; no selection from an empty set is required.

The Statement fixes L>0 and the Picard series indexed by n>=0, so its index family is nonempty and includes u_0=p. At x=x_0 the Volterra integrals and their triangular integration domains have zero length and integral zero in step 1.1; step 4.1 has the same zero-length behavior for all positive iterates. Empty partial sums are zero and do not remove the separate initial term p (or c_1 in the derivative series).

The null-set intersection defining H_ac includes the empty Borel set, whose PVM projection is zero, so that member imposes no restriction. Compact sources may be g=0 with empty support: F3 gives mu_0=0, and the kernel, density and cutoff arguments in steps 3.1, 6.1-8.1 then vanish. Step 3.2 permits a zero-rank negative band: its basis sum is empty, nu=0, and no nonzero support point is asserted.

The real positive-energy Wronskian is nonzero by the stated Jost interface F2, while step 2.1 proves the nonreal Wronskian nonzero before the Green denominator in step 3.1. Step 1.2 excludes the zero-energy eigenvector separately for gamma>0 and gamma=0. Steps 7.1 and 8.1 exclude all positive atoms, including for the zero source.

The l=0 channel is included by the endpoint/form argument of step 1.1 and the zero-exclusion argument of step 1.2. Step 2.2 allows rank-one negative spectral bands and step 3.2 treats their finite basis/support argument. No special normalization at E=1 is used.

Step 2.1 excludes a nonreal Wronskian zero by self-adjointness; F2 excludes real k>0 zeros. Step 1.2 handles gamma=0 without division by gamma, and step 3.2 gives zero negative projection for that case. Zero-dimensional negative band ranges are allowed in the finite-rank argument.

Step 1.1 establishes form membership at r=0 and radial infinity by cutoffs. Step 1.2 excludes an atom at energy 0. Steps 7.1-8.1 exclude positive atoms before step 9.1 takes the interval Poisson limit, so its half-weight endpoint terms vanish. No uniform density bound at E=0 or E=infinity is asserted.

The Statement retains AC and CC. Step 2.2 uses AC only to select an orthonormal sequence if a negative band were infinite dimensional; step 3.2 uses a finite basis when its dimension is positive. Step 8.1 uses the explicit cutoffs g_n=1_[1/n,n] g and needs no additional selection; zero-rank bands use the empty basis.

For the equality H_ac(A_l)=E_A_l((0,infinity))L2 in clause (d), step 10.1 shows an absolutely continuous scalar measure gives zero mass to the countable negative support of step 3.2 and to {0}, hence the vector lies in the positive subspace.

For the reverse inclusion in clause (d), step 8.1 proves positive-energy restrictions of every scalar measure absolutely continuous; step 9.2 applies this to positive-subspace vectors, whose entire measures are positive-supported, and step 10.1 concludes the equality.

Step 1.1 permits M=0 and z=0 in its tensor-continuity estimate; step 1.2 gives 0 tensor I=0. Step 3.1 includes the zero simple function and zero bounded function. Step 3.2 explicitly handles m=0 or C=0, hence z_0=0 and the zero scalar measure; step 4.1 separately handles z=0.

Step 1.1 permits zero limiting operators and M=0. Step 3.2 handles empty finite tensors and C=0 before dividing by mC. Step 4.1 handles the zero vector before its density/regularity estimates; no nonzero scalar mass is presumed.

Step 1.1 gives W_0=-2i/h with h>0, hence W_0!=0 and |W_0|=2/h; F3 and step 5.1 give p>=sqrt(delta)>0. The quotient q/W_0 therefore has no zero-denominator branch. Step 2.1 includes c(a)=0 without division by its norm; step 3.1 explicitly includes c(a)=0, and step 4.1 then gives zero wavefunction error. For x=a, the integrals vanish and both deviation/error bounds are zero.

The estimates are valid for every h>0, including h=1: step 1.1 derives the exact matrix norm and steps 2.1-4.1 integrate it without a small-h assumption. Step 5.1 separately qualifies when the bound is small.

F3 gives the positive p gap on the entire closed interval. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 integrate from a to every x in [a,b], including x=a with zero integrals and x=b with finite integrals; step 4.1 transfers the corresponding pointwise bound.

CC is retained as declared by the physical model and relevant supplier hypotheses. Step 1.1 constructs c explicitly from the invertible matrix; steps 2.1-4.1 derive the estimates directly using F2. No coefficient vector is selected from an empty family and no extra choice is introduced.
